![[5qn1vfg7jy5ynj1fbmyzqsfjyb]]

Very interesting read.

The guest author defines a Factory as:
- Shared — multiple people on the team can use them.

- Specific — they are optimized to handle certain types of recurring tasks, unlike a general-purpose agent.

- Scrutinized — some people on the team can see the work flowing through the factory to observe and fix failures.

I think I already have factories at home, in close to the ideal form factor for legibility at this stage of agentic evolution.

Each of my specialized [Spacebot](https://spacebot.sh) agents is defined by a section in a toml file (inference provider waterfall), a handful of `SOUL.md` style Markdown files, its own collection of Claude skills, and participation in any number of Discord, Slack, SMS and email channels.

For example, I have a `slides-maker` agent, with specialized skills to make presentations and deploy them as a simple static site. Anyone in the team in Discord/Slack can ping the agent. It has its own API keys and token budget, in addition to its unique skills and personality. And team members can observe/control the agent, at various levels of permissioning.

There's another one for `deep-research` which has its own API keys and budget to use services, as well as compartmentalized bulkhead memory so researched topics don't leak to the `slides-maker` agent unless they message each other.

In the context of personal agents vs factories, these specialized, partially isolated agents appear to be mini factories.

It seems that one can turn a personal agent platform into factories by scaling them horizontally and giving them enhanced capabilities vertically.
